facts.text: The Seed helper posts six Widget facts and returns a World record carrying the input, revised, stale, claim, refuter and plain fact ids.
at: return new World(input, revised, stale, claim, refuter, plain);

facts.text: The Statuses helper projects search hits into a dictionary from each hit id to that hit's status string.
A Search over the seeded Widget subject returns 5 hits, with the stale fact stale, the claim contested, and the superseded input absent.
SearchBrief with Brief set returns the same stale and contested statuses on its hits.
at: var brief = db.Store.SearchBrief(new SearchRequest { Subject = "Widget", Brief = true });

facts.text: A Search with Status live over the seeded subject reports Total 3 and includes only live hits.
The status filter combines with a text query: Q delivery with Status stale returns 1 hit and with Status live returns 0.
A stale filter paged at Limit 2 walks the 5 stale ids in order and reports Total 5 with Complete false.
Two facts declaring headerHeight 64 and 72 both stay live while Compile reports 1 conflict.
A refutes ref makes the first data fact contested, yet the conflict still lists both facts and Check counts 1 conflict.
Compile for the seeded subject with Recency 0 returns 5 facts and places the stale fact last despite the need matching it best.
The stale fact's single why entry carries Rel derived_from, State superseded and ReplacedBy the revised fact id.
Under BudgetMode strict with Budget 260, some facts are emitted and some dropped, and no stale fact is emitted while a live one was dropped.
The rendered markdown line for the stale fact contains stale: plus both the input and revised fact ids.
UsedTokens equals the sum of EstimateFactTokens over every emitted fact in markdown format, status marks included.
Show on the stale fact reports status stale with a null ReplacedBy, while the superseded input names the revised fact.
Serializing a plain Show result omits the why and replaced_by keys entirely.
Verify across the Tangle fixture yields every one of live, superseded, retracted, stale and contested.
Repeated compiles of one request serialize identically, and the result holds 4 facts ending with stale lines.
In strict clustering the live near-duplicate of a stale fact does not cite it, and the stale fact stays in the dossier.
A facts row hand-updated to status stale still reads live in Show and in a Search with Status live.
After importing a bundle, no facts row holds a status other than live and the fact that was stale arrives reading live.
at: await Assert.That(Fixtures.Count(connection, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM facts WHERE status NOT IN ('live')")).IsEqualTo(0);

facts.text: The search probe fires 1 time and the page excludes the id posted while the search was running.
With Budget 80 the oversized live fact and the tiny stale fact are both dropped, while the revised input is emitted.
A published index page carries no stale or contested status note and charges only the plain line token total.
The store schema creates the indexes idx_refs_currency and idx_facts_slot.
With 2000 derived conclusions the stale filter totals 2000, and Compile lists every live fact before any stale one.
A Status superseded filter over the seeded subject returns only the superseded input fact, with status superseded.
Show on the contested claim lists the refuter as its single inbound fact.
Superseded and retracted facts are absent from both Search and Compile results, while the other statuses agree with Verify.
The search after the write finds the derived fact and the late conclusion both stale.
A live fact verifies as Current while the response Revision equals the store revision.
When a keyed fact is posted again, each earlier version is superseded and names the newest post as ReplacedBy.
A superseded fact whose successor was retracted reports a null ReplacedBy, and the successor reads retracted.
An unknown id is reported with status unknown and a null SubjectId rather than thrown, and Current becomes false.
A derived fact whose input was superseded by a different claim reports why rel derived_from and state superseded.
Staleness reaches the leaf transitively, and the leaf's why names its direct input with state stale and a null ReplacedBy.
A tag-only repost returns status replaced while the derived fact stays live with no why.
Retracting an input makes its derived fact stale with why state retracted and a null ReplacedBy.
A mention or a supports ref to a superseded fact leaves the referring fact live.
A hand-inserted derived_from cycle terminates, and both members read stale whichever order they are asked in.
A derived_from ref to a fact id absent from the store leaves the fact live with no why.
A refuted fact is contested with why rel refutes naming the refuter, while the refuter itself stays live.
A contradicts ref marks both facts contested, each fact's why naming the other.
A dispute ends when the refuter is retracted, when a keyed objection is reposted without the ref, or when the refuter's derived input changes.
Stale outranks contested, and a fresh post on the same key turns the derived fact superseded with a null why.
Exec sets a facts row status to stale through raw SQL, after which Verify still reads that fact as live.
at: Exec(db, "UPDATE facts SET status = 'stale' WHERE id = $id", ("$id", id));

facts.text: Verify of one id repeated returns a single fact and leaves the store revision unchanged.
Verify throws invalid_request for an empty request, a blank id, or more than MaxVerifyIds ids.
The listed verify_facts tool has ids as its first required field and a description mentioning untrusted data.
A verify_facts call with an empty ids array answers isError true and text containing invalid_request.
CLI verify with --require-current on a live fact exits 0 and prints JSON whose current is true.
CLI verify with --require-current on a stale fact exits 1 and writes not current to stderr.
A misspelled option --require-curent makes CLI verify exit 1 with an unknown option error.
The Run helper starts Dossier.dll with DOSSIER_DB set to the database path and returns exit code, stdout and stderr.
